summary: Authored the exploratory lifetime-objective namespace: an instrumented whole-game harness with an enforced score-decomposition identity, a parameterized fair search proved decision-identical to the frozen reference, a survival-labelled corpus generator with all-legal-sibling panels, and a GPU training pipeline targeting survival hazard rather than score. Measured the score decomposition of fair D4 on fresh seeds and established the disc-conservation flow-balance requirement. Ran and reported the terminal-utility and chance-strata sweeps.
validationPerformed: CHECK gate: the parameterized depth-4 search reproduced chooseDepth4Action exactly, 50 moves compared, 0 mismatches.
Score-decomposition identity score == 17000*rises + 70000*clears + sum(waveDepthPoints) asserted per game and held for 64/64 fair-D4 games and 192/192 trivial-policy games.

Dataset reader validated against a real generated corpus: record layout matches the C++ packed struct at 72 bytes, chosen column always legal, movesToDeath strictly decrements within a game, one-hot planes sum to one, whole-origin splits disjoint.
limitations: All output is exploratory and lives in a separate namespace; it does not upgrade docs/research/ or any frozen protocol.
64 paired games per arm on one exploratory lease; the score standard deviation is 58 percent of the mean, so single-cohort deltas are weak evidence.

The 7-strata arm required raising the frozen 3,200,000 work bound to 16,000,000 because worst-case depth-4 work at seven strata is 11,892,398; results at the frozen bound would silently be a completed depth-3 search.
Figures describe this repository's simulator, including the two rise-boundary scoring discrepancies recorded in docs/exploratory/audit-01-engine-fidelity.md.
The training pipeline is written and layout-validated but has not yet been trained or evaluated.
